title: Causes of the Second World War
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:52Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point covers all four causes together, including the Depression and German resentment of Versailles, and no bank point covers that full set at Year 10 depth: the closest, the road to the Second World War, omits the Depression and the resentment of Versailles.

draft.title: Causes of the Second World War
card: The Treaty of Versailles (1919) ended the First World War. Many Germans resented it because it blamed Germany for the war, took land and made it pay reparations.
The Great Depression of the 1930s caused mass unemployment. Many people turned to leaders who promised strength and action, such as Adolf Hitler in Germany.
Germany, Italy and Japan used force to expand. Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931, Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935, and Germany took over Austria and Czechoslovakia.
Britain and France followed a policy of appeasement. They gave in to some demands, hoping to avoid another war. It did not stop the aggression.
draft.remember: Anger over Versailles, the Depression, aggression and appeasement together led to war.

a.q: Britain and France let Hitler take over parts of Czechoslovakia in 1938, hoping to keep the peace. What is this policy called?
a.why: Appeasement means giving in to demands to avoid war. Aggression describes what Hitler did by using force and threats. It does not describe the response of Britain and France.
a.clue: Think about giving in to avoid conflict.

b.q: Which event helped Hitler gain support in Germany in the early 1930s?
opts: Mass unemployment during the Great Depression
Britain's policy of appeasement towards Germany
b.why: The Depression left many Germans jobless and angry, and some turned to Hitler's promises. Appeasement and the invasions of Ethiopia and Manchuria are real causes of the war, but they came after or alongside his rise to power.
b.clue: Which one hit ordinary Germans' daily lives?

b.best: Mass unemployment during the Great Depression
